## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ubhatobhaṭṭhajātaka* (Ja 139), translated as "A Twofold Failure", is a narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection. According to the commentary, the story begins with the verse opening *Akkhī bhinnā paṭo naṭṭho ti* and was delivered by the Buddha while residing at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana) concerning Devadatta [Fausböll 1877]. The narrative frame opens with the monks assembled in the Hall of Truth (*dhammasabhā*) discussing Devadatta's fate: just as a brand from a funeral pyre charred at both ends and fouled in the middle (*chavālātaṃ ubhato padittaṃ majjhe gūthagataṃ*) is useless as timber in both forest and village, so Devadatta suffered a twofold failure by abandoning the comforts of lay life while falling short of his religious vocation as a monastic [Fausböll 1877].

  The Pali text and commentary were edited by V. Fausböll in the first volume of his edition of the *Jātaka* [Fausböll 1877].
